correctness.rationale: For every finite height-at-most-two poset, radical-square-zero incidence multiplication gives (aba)_{uv}=(d_uc_u+d_vc_v)x_{uv}+d_ud_v y_{uv} and d_v^2c_v=d_v. Choosing c_v as the inverse of each nonzero d_v proves regularity iff every edge with both diagonal endpoints zero has zero coefficient; the explicit y_{uv} solves all remaining equations in every characteristic. Summing the disjoint zero-diagonal strata yields the stated regular-element polynomial. Inclusion-exclusion over forbidden edge events gives an exact subgraph sum, and triangle-freeness proves the incident-edge-pair coefficient in the large-q expansion. Enumerating the 16 zero sets on each four-vertex graph gives the two polynomials and difference \(q(q-1)^3\). Independent brute-force linear-system solving of aba=a for every algebra element over F2, F3 and F4 matches counts 89/91, 1777/1801, 14377/14485. Finite checks do not replace the infinite proof.

value.rationale: This addresses whether the strong family of all-arity commuting-idempotent counts suffices to distinguish incidence algebras. The answer is sharply negative even on the four-vertex tree pair: exact von Neumann regular-element frequencies are different in every finite characteristic, by \(q(q-1)^3\). A general induced-edge formula identifies the mechanism and extracts the incident-edge-pair statistic from asymptotic density. Regularity is a natural algebraic invariant and tree-vs-tree matroid blindness is a motivated structural boundary, not an arbitrary slice or a known numerical table recomputation.
